Executive Summary
Create a Roblox Demonfall-inspired open-world action RPG set in a Taishō-era fantasy. The player starts as a human in a rural earth-biome village, returns home to find their family slain by a demon, then splinters into two paths: Survive = become a Slayer, Die = become a Demon. A cinematic prologue and mobile-friendly obby tutorial teach basic movement (run, jump, camera), combat (light/heavy attack, block, dash), and UI (controls overlay before drawing the katana). Players choose a family (clan) with unique buffs and cosmetic style during character creation (e.g. Kanroji clan gives +15% damage, Kamado clan +20% EXP and Sun-immunity). The core gameplay loop emphasizes dynamic combat with stamina/breathing management, deep progression (skill tree, breathing styles, Blood Demon Arts), cooperative PvE missions (with scalable difficulty), and a day/night cycle that makes nights dangerous (demons hunt; they die in daylight without Sun immunity).

Key Systems:

Combat: Simple mobile controls (touch buttons) and PC controls (keyboard/mouse) for light/heavy slash, block, dash/sprint, weapon draw/sheath, plus a visible Stamina/Breath meter. Advanced skills are unlocked via breathing styles (9-12 styles) or demon arts.
Progression: Players earn skill points by killing demons, completing quests, and conquering missions. A branching skill tree lets them improve stats (Strength, Endurance, Speed, Steel-Lungs to slow breathing drain, Dash upgrades, etc.) and unlock special moves.
Breathing Styles (Slayer paths): At least ten breathing arts (Water, Flame, Thunder, Wind, Mist, Stone, Love, Serpent, Sound, Beast, plus secret Sun/Moon) exist, each with trainer NPCs and unlock quests. Four beginner-friendly styles (Water, Flame, Thunder, Beast) are accessible early; higher-tier styles require harder quests or demos. For example, Beast Breathing (dual-wield style) requires Level 10, 10,000 Yen, dual katanas and a hidden mountain cave trainer. Clan synergy is important: e.g., Hashibira clan grants +10% damage for Beast users.
Demon Path: If a player dies in the prologue, they become a demon with regeneration, Blood Arts, and increased power. Demons climb their own boss ladder (ordinary demons → Demon Ranks → Lower Moon bosses → Upper Moon bosses). Slayer players may choose to become demons by consuming Muzan's blood (a rare item or boss drop) and waiting in "hybrid" limbo (taking real-time hours based on level). Conversely, demons can revert via a rare Wipe Potion sold by a special merchant, or by codes, reflecting community lore.
World & Quests: A large open map (see World Map diagram below) connects varied zones: the Starting Village (tutorial area), Cursed Forests (moonlit wood with fog), Snowy Mountain Pass (Beast trainer), Butterfly Mansion (advanced training/Full Concentration skill), Swordsmith Village/Forge, Haunted Roads (night raids), Spider Mountain Caves (elite slayer boss), and an Endgame Fortress (final raids). Day/night cycles and weather (fog, rain, moonlight) dynamically affect visibility and demon behavior. NPCs follow schedules (working/closing shops in day, hiding at night), and random events (e.g. demon attacks on a caravan, lost child rescues, or chance boss spawns) create a living world. Quests include daily hunts, escort/defense missions, boss investigations, and special trials. Party missions auto-scale: more players = tougher enemies and better rewards.
Building & Tech: The design is modular for Roblox Build. We define core modules (Combat, Movement, UI, etc.) and RemoteEvents for communication. Development is phased: 1) Foundation: world base, controls, spawn points, character/family selection, tutorial obby. 2) Core Combat: weapon equip, attacks, block, dodge, enemy AI, stamina. 3) Progression & Quests: skill tree, breathing trainers, basic quests, party system. 4) World Expansion: add villages, NPCs, day/night, weather, merchant, Butterfly Mansion. 5) Endgame: boss fights (Lower/Upper Moons, Hashira mentors), transformation routes, secret rewards. 6) Polish: UI/UX, effects, sound/music, performance tweaks (especially mobile).

Below are detailed system designs, tables and diagrams to fully specify each element, so that a Roblox Build AI can be instructed to generate the game coherently. Citations reference real Demonfall community knowledge and lore to ground the design in player expectations.

World Layout and Progression
The world is a connected open map with natural transitions. Players first train in the Starting Village (Earth Biome), then venture into increasingly dangerous zones. A sample progression path is:

mermaid
Копировать
flowchart LR
 A[Starting Village (earth biome)] --> B[Foggy Forest of Moonlit Hunts]
 B --> C[Butterfly Mansion (slayer HQ)]
 C --> D[Swordsmith Forge Village]
 B --> E[Snowy Mountain Pass (Beast Trainer)]
 D --> F[Haunted Road (night demon ambush)]
 F --> G[Spider Demon Caves (Lower Moon boss)]
 G --> H[Endgame Demon Fortress (Upper Moon boss)] 
 H --> A
Starting Village (Earth Biome): Safe zone by day; acts as hub. Families roll here, obby tutorial and controls demo are here.
Foggy Forest & Moonlit Hunts: Shaded woods around village. By night, demons roam; civilians lock doors. Players hunt weaker demons (R1-R10 ranks). At dusk, random hunts or caravan assaults occur.
Butterfly Mansion (Training Area): A separate fantasy mansion zone where players can learn Full Concentration (max breath bar skill) via an advanced trainer. Also a healer NPC and story mentor appear.
Forge Village / Hayakawa: A blacksmith village with a crafting system (weapon upgrades, repairs). Also home to some trainers (e.g. Wind Breathing Trainer).
Snowy Mountain Pass: Alpine trails, where the Beast Breathing Trainer hides in a cave. Contains boulder-obstacle parkour. Cold weather adds atmosphere.
Haunted Road: Dark, rural road where ambush quests (escort villagers, defend against demon waves) happen.
Spider Demon Caves: Mid-game boss arena for Spider Demon (Lower Moon 6). Twisting tunnels to explore. Rewards special materials.
Endgame Demon Fortress / Summit: Icy fortress in highest mountains. Final Upper Moon bosses and minibosses spawn here. Challenging raid content.
Day/Night Cycle: Demonfall had a day/night cycle reinstated. Here, night strengthens demons (higher spawn rate, they gain stealth). Demons (without Sun immunity) take damage or die in daylight, so survivors flee or burn at dawn. Weather effects (rain reduces visibility, heavy fog delays sight) add tactical depth. For example, fog can hide a rare demon or make parkour harder. Townsfolk NPC schedules add life (e.g., shops close at night, guards patrol).

World Map Flow (Mermaid Diagram)
mermaid
Копировать
flowchart TD
 SV[Starting Village] --> Fog[Foggy Forest]
 SV --> WV[Woodland Path (day) / Haunted Road (night)]
 Fog --> BF[Butterfly Mansion Zone]
 WV --> Forge[Swordsmith Village]
 Fog --> Mountain[Snowy Mountain Pass]
 Forge --> Caves[Spider Demon Caves]
 Mountain --> Caves
 Caves --> Fortress[Endgame Fortress]
 Fortress --> SV
This illustrates travel routes and unlocking: e.g., after mastering basic breaths, players can climb to the Mountain; after lower moons, unlock Fortress quests.

Family (Clan) System
At character creation, players choose a family/surname (based on Demon Slayer clans). Each clan grants passive buffs and cosmetic flair. Families are tiered by rarity (common vs. rare 0.5%-2%). Examples (drawn from Demonfall wiki/Reddit) include:

Family (Clan) Rarity Buffs/Perks
Kanroji (Kocho) 2% +15% damage to all attacks (katana and breathing).
Kamado 0.5% +20% EXP gain, +1 Sun Breathing form (if slayer), sunlight immunity as demon/hybrid.
Tomioka 1% Free Lunge and Shoulder Bash skills at start (+2 extra SP). (Deep Calm 11th form move if slayer.)
Agatsuma (Zenitsu) 2% (Suggested) Faster M1 attacks or faster Thunder skill cooldown.
Shinazugawa 1% (Inspired) Large HP or Poise increase; fearsome appearance (e.g. a bandage mask).
Hashibira (Inosuke) 1% Increased heal and movement rate in combat (faster regen); unique boar mask cosmetic.
Uzui (Sound) 2% (Suggested) Slight XP boost or increased drop chance, reflecting Uzui's festival wealth.
Kanroji (Mist) 2% 15% damage buff (same as Kocho listed above, Mist-Kanroji).
Himejima (Gyomei) 1% High Strength: e.g. +10% base strength or armor. (Hashira-highest HP.)
Tokito (Mist) 2% Breath regen bonus, faster skill cooldown on Mist breathing moves.
Kocho (Insect) 2% Health regen speed or poison resistance (thematically Insect).
Hashibira (Swap) 2% Worst according to players; no direct stat buff, possibly negative (fast hunger). (This matches Ubuyashiki lore: +10% XP, 2 SP but perma-burn penalty.)

Notes on buffs: These values come from community data and lore. For instance, Kanroji clan "deals +15% Damage on EVERYTHING". Kamado clan "gives +20% exp buff" and "sunlight immunity" for hybrids. We mirror these in our design: families should clearly show their bonuses in the UI when chosen. The table above should expand to include all canonical clans in final prompt.

Breathing Styles & Unlocks
The Slayer path centers on learning Breathing Styles. We classify them by difficulty tier:

Beginner Tier (easy unlock): Water, Flame, Thunder, Beast.
Mid Tier: Wind, Mist, Stone, Love, Serpent, Sound.
Advanced Tier: Insect, Moon, Secret Sun (requires special conditions), future Hybrids.
Each style has a trainer NPC and specific unlock requirements (level, currency, mission). For example, Beast Breathing (Inosuke's style) in Demonfall requires: Level ≥10, 10,000 Yen, Dual Nichirin Swords (obtained from the forge), and speaking to the Beast Trainer in a hidden mountain cave. The trainer's location can require a small navigation or parkour challenge, fitting the lore (e.g. "in a remote cave obscured by bushes"). Once requirements are met, the player pays a fee or completes a mini-quest (e.g. defeating wild beasts), then learns the new style.

For each style, the prompt will list: Trainer Location, Unlock Requirements, Quest Outline, and a brief moveset description. For example:

Breathing Style Trainer / Location Requirements Moveset Highlights
Water Urokodaki in Coast Forest (house w/ boulder) 1,000 Yen, Intro tutorial completed M1: Striking Tide (horizontal slash); M2: Water Wheel (charged swing); M3: Whirlpool (AoE). Passive: breath regen per M1.
Flame Rengoku atop White Peak ~2,000 Yen, defeat smaller fire demon M1: Unknowing Fire (slash), M2: Rising Fire (axe swing), M3: Fire Burst (explosion).
Thunder Zenitsu's mentor in Thunder Shrine 1,500 Yen, Sprint trial completed M1: Thunderclap (fast stab), M2: Ram (shoulder dash), M3: Raijin (AoE shockwave).
Beast Beast Trainer in Hidden Mountain Cave Lvl≥10, 10,000 Yen, Dual Katanas Fangs: Lunge (guard-break), Devour (combo), Spatial Awareness buff (7th Fang).
Mist Tokito's shrine in Mist Village Lvl≥15, 15,000 Yen, forest obby challenge M1: Barrage, M2: Judgment Cut, M3: True Flow. Good for dodging.
Wind Temple in Cloud Mountain (Uzui area) Lvl≥20, 20,000 Yen, windmill climbing challenge Fast M1 combo, M2 Spinning Edge, M3 Gale.
Stone Gyomei's shrine on Sacred Peak Lvl≥25, 25,000 Yen, break stone pillars quest Heavy M1, Earthshaker slam, Ground Split AoE.
Love Mitsuri's garden sanctuary Lvl≥30, 30,000 Yen, heart-building quest (help NPC) Ribbon strike M1, Love Barrage, Vine grasp.
Serpent Obanai's hidden garden Lvl≥40, 40,000 Yen, sneak through vines quest Constrict M1, Venom M2 (dot), Snake Pit AoE.
Sound Uzui's mansion fortress Lvl≥45, 45,000 Yen, rhythm game trial Drum thrust M1, Spark Sound M2 (projectile), Fisticuffs M3.
Insect Shinobu's butterfly mansion Lvl≥50, 50,000 Yen, timed bug-catching trial Needle M1, Poison Cloud M2, Cocoon M3 (trap).
Moon (Demon Hybrid) Kokushibo (Upper Moon 1) Must be Hybrid (demon+slayer), defeat Upper Moon Ultra-powerful moves (game finale).
Sun (Secret) Tanjiro's secret dojo (legend only) Special long quest + high prestige All-around ultimate combo style.

(The exact numbers/quests above are suggestions; the prompt should allow Roblox AI to fill specifics.)

Each breathing style's acquisition should use quest templates. For example, unlocking a style might require "Kill X demons in Y minutes", "Collect Z rare items from monsters", or "Survive N minutes on a night patrol without dying". We will define at least 10 templates and rotate them. For example:

Timed Hunt: "Slay 20 demons within 10 minutes."
Horn Gathering: "Collect 50 Demon Horns dropped by Night Demons."
Boss Duel: "Challenge a mini-boss (e.g. Demon Rank 5) solo, no deaths."
Stealth Trial: "Escort NPC through forest without alerting demons."
Wave Defense: "Survive 3 waves of attacking demons at a lookout."
Escort Mission: "Guard a merchant caravan for 5 minutes."
Timed Parkour: "Reach the mountaintop within 3 minutes (obstacle course)."
Elite Slayers Assist: "Join an elite Slayer NPC to defeat 5 demons."
Item Delivery: "Retrieve a legendary ore from mines for the blacksmith."
Puzzle/Trial: "Solve the runes at Butterfly Mansion to unlock skill."
These quests are reused for different styles by changing numbers, enemy types, or locations. The prompt will instruct the AI to randomize numbers each time or pick appropriate spawn zones.

Demon Path and Transformations
If the player's prologue "boss" demon wins, the player becomes a Demon. Demons have: auto HP regen, extra mobility, and unique Blood Arts (special skills). The demon progression ladder is:

Minor Demons (random spawns, weaker).
Demon Ranks 1-10 (named demonic fighters).
Lower Moon Bosses 6-1.
Upper Moon Bosses 5-1 (team raids).
Muzan (Ultimate Demon Lord) optional endgame fight.
Players can switch sides mid-game:

A Slayer → Demon requires Muzan's Blood (quest reward or rare merchant item) and a timed "corruption" (24 real-hours that can speed up with level). High-level Slayers (w/ breathing) become a Hybrid demon (Sun-breathing enabled, lore nod to Kokushibo/Kyogai).
A Demon → Slayer can happen via a Wipe Potion (sold by a rare NPC for high cost, or via achievement/quest), which resets your demon state and lets you join the Corps. Demons get exclusive quests (hunt high-value humans, ambush missions) and rewards (demon points, Blood Demon Art unlocks).
Death in normal play is lenient: players simply respawn at their chosen village spawn point with slight penalties (lost time only). Only the introductory fight converts the character.

Quest and Mission System
Missions are accepted from quest boards or NPCs in villages. They auto-complete for party members. Major mission types:

Hunt Missions: Kill X demons in region.
Defense Missions: Defend an NPC/building from waves.
Escort Missions: Protect a villager or merchant.
Investigation Missions: Solve a mystery (find missing person, track demon tracks).
Boss Missions: Unlock and fight a specific Lower/Upper Moon boss (requires group).
Survival Missions: Survive a time period on Demon-infested road.
Dungeon Raids: Clear an enemy camp/cave for loot.
A mission UI lets players select, track progress, and see rewards (currency, XP, skill points, special items).

Boss Ladder
Design bosses in tiers, reflecting Demonfall's Lower/Upper Moons. At least include Lower Moon 6→1, Upper Moon 5→1, plus optional Hashira rivals. Each boss has unique mechanics (e.g. blind spots, minion adds, stage phases). Key bosses: Spider Demon (Lower 6), Bountiful Demon (multi-boss Lower 5), (Lower 1-3 as in series), then Upper Moons like Nakime (teleport map), Gyokko (water demon), Kokushibo (endgame hybrid boss), Muzan (final final). Defeating each yields rare drops (unique abilities or crafting mats).

UI Design
A mobile-first UI with a mirrored PC layout:

Main Screen (HUD): Top corners: minimap (with quest markers). Bottom left: movement joystick (mobile), invisible on PC. Bottom right: four large buttons (Light Attack, Heavy Attack, Dodge/Dash, Block). A Breathing/Buff meter (like "Ki bar") floats near ability buttons. UI should be legible for one-thumb play.

Controls Overlay: Before drawing katana, show an overlay image describing control scheme (mobile and PC). Example labels in Russian: "Нажмите ✤ для лёгкой атаки, □ для блока". Once dismissed, player gets the katana.

Character Creation Screen: Input name, select family (show family banners with buff icons, e.g. +15% DMG). Show preview of avatar. Simple mobile navigation (arrows or swipe).

Spawn/Revival Screen: Let player set their spawn village (applied each death).

Skill Tree UI: Grid with nodes (Breath styles, Strength, Stamina, special moves). Tapping a node shows name, description, cost in points. Branching tree lines. Accessible via menu.

Breathing Styles Screen: List unlocked styles and locked ones (with "How to unlock" tips).

Quest Log: Scrollable list of active/available quests, with objectives and map markers.

Map: Full-screen regional map with icons (towns, trainers, quest locations, bosses). Zoomable on PC, pinch on mobile.

Inventory: Item slots, currency, equip weapon/amulets. Consumables (potions) quick-access.

Party Panel: Shows party members (health bars, revive option). Button to invite/join party.

Settings: Includes Mobile Control Editor: allow players to reposition on-screen buttons. PC controls listed as reference.

Example Russian UI text:

"Выберите фамилию" above family selection.
"Обучение дыханию: найти Учителя Воды" in quest prompt.
Attack button labeled "Удар".
(These Russian bits are just illustrative; main prompt stays English.)

Technical Architecture
Structure the game in modules with clear folder/script hierarchy. For example:

bash
Копировать
Workspace
 - Terrain, MapParts
ReplicatedStorage
 - Modules
 • CombatModule (functions for damage, parry, etc.)
 • MovementModule (sprint, dash, jump)
 • ControlModule (input handling, mobile vs PC)
 • BreathingModule (style stats, unlock logic)
 • DemonModule (blood arts, transformation)
 • QuestModule (quest templates, progress tracking)
 • NPCModule (ai behaviors, vendors, trainers)
 • BossModule (boss AI states/phases)
 • InventoryModule
 • SkillTreeModule (node data, apply upgrades)
 • PartyModule (sync group status, revive)
 • UI Module (menu handling, tooltips)
 • AudioModule (ambient/music cues)
 • WorldEventsModule (day/night cycle, random spawns)
 - Remotes
 • RemoteEvent_Attack
 • RemoteEvent_Defend
 • RemoteFunction_GetStatus
 • RemoteEvent_StartQuest
 • ...
 - Scripts (server)
 • Server/GameManager (initializes world, day/night)
 • Server/SpawnManager (handles respawns)
 • Server/NPCSpawner (spawns demons based on time)
 • Server/QuestManager
 - LocalScripts (client)
 • Client/CameraController
 • Client/UIManager
 • Client/InputManager
 • Client/PlayerStats (updates HUD)
RemoteEvents/Functions Examples:

RemoteEvent_DoMeleeAttack(player, targetID) - called by client to execute a slash.
RemoteFunction_CheckQuestProgress(player) - returns progress data.
RemoteEvent_TransformToDemon(player) - triggers demon-mode on server.
We must optimize: low-detail meshes, LOD for distant objects, mobile-friendly particle counts. Use simple lighting, avoid too many simultaneous particles. Day/night could be a single time-of-day skybox blend.

Development Phases & Roadmap
Plan sprints/phases (illustrated in chart below). Each phase builds on last; features added incrementally.

Phase Features Estimated Scope
1: Foundation Map prototype, movement (mobile/PC), camera, UI basics, spawn/respawn, char. creation & family selection, tutorial obby ★★☆☆☆ (20%)
2: Core Combat Katana equip/draw, basic attacks (light/heavy), stamina system, blocking, dodging, enemy NPC AI (basic demons), health system ★★★☆☆ (25%)
3: Progression Quest board and simple quests (slayer & demon), skill point & tree system, first breathing style trainer (e.g. Water), stat upgrades, simple

answers.ask: Should the eight zones be one continuous world, or separate maps stitched by loading transitions?
answers.answer: Use one continuous open world with natural transitions between all eight zones, as specified in the world layout.

answers.ask: Are the caves and the fortress instanced per party, or shared open world?
answers.answer: Make Spider Demon Caves and the Endgame Demon Fortress instanced per party so their boss encounters, scaling, and raid progression work cleanly.

For example, Beast Breathing (Inosuke's style) in Demonfall requires: Level ≥10, 10,000 Yen, Dual Nichirin Swords (obtained from the forge), and speaking to the Beast Trainer in a hidden mountain cave. The trainer's location can require a small navigation or parkour challenge, fitting the lore (e.g. "in a remote cave obscured by bushes"). Once requirements are met, the player pays a fee or completes a mini-quest (e.g. defeating wild beasts), then learns the new style.

Demon Path and Transformations
If the player's prologue "boss" demon wins, the player becomes a Demon. Demons have: auto HP regen, extra mobility, and unique Blood Arts (special skills). The demon progression ladder is:

Minor Demons (random spawns, weaker).
Demon Ranks 1-10 (named demonic fighters).
Lower Moon Bosses 6-1.
Upper Moon Bosses 5-1 (team raids).
Muzan (Ultimate Demon Lord) optional endgame fight.
Players can switch sides mid-game:

A Slayer → Demon requires Muzan's Blood (quest reward or rare merchant item) and a timed "corruption" (24 real-hours that can speed up with level). High-level Slayers (w/ breathing) become a Hybrid demon (Sun-breathing enabled, lore nod to Kokushibo/Kyogai).
A Demon → Slayer can happen via a Wipe Potion (sold by a rare NPC for high cost, or via achievement/quest), which resets your demon state and lets you join the Corps. Demons get exclusive quests (hunt high-value humans, ambush missions) and rewards (demon points, Blood Demon Art unlocks).
Death in normal play is lenient: players simply respawn at their chosen village spawn point with slight penalties (lost time only). Only the introductory fight converts the character.

Quest and Mission System
Missions are accepted from quest boards or NPCs in villages. They auto-complete for party members. Major mission types:

Hunt Missions: Kill X demons in region.
Defense Missions: Defend an NPC/building from waves.
Escort Missions: Protect a villager or merchant.
Investigation Missions: Solve a mystery (find missing person, track demon tracks).
Boss Missions: Unlock and fight a specific Lower/Upper Moon boss (requires group).
Survival Missions: Survive a time period on Demon-infested road.
Dungeon Raids: Clear an enemy camp/cave for loot.
A mission UI lets players select, track progress, and see rewards (currency, XP, skill points, special items).

Boss Ladder
Design bosses in tiers, reflecting Demonfall's Lower/Upper Moons. At least include Lower Moon 6→1, Upper Moon 5→1, plus optional Hashira rivals. Each boss has unique mechanics (e.g. blind spots, minion adds, stage phases). Key bosses: Spider Demon (Lower 6), Bountiful Demon (multi-boss Lower 5), (Lower 1-3 as in series), then Upper Moons like Nakime (teleport map), Gyokko (water demon), Kokushibo (endgame hybrid boss), Muzan (final final). Defeating each yields rare drops (unique abilities or crafting mats).

UI Design
A mobile-first UI with a mirrored PC layout:

Main Screen (HUD): Top corners: minimap (with quest markers). Bottom left: movement joystick (mobile), invisible on PC. Bottom right: four large buttons (Light Attack, Heavy Attack, Dodge/Dash, Block). A Breathing/Buff meter (like "Ki bar") floats near ability buttons. UI should be legible for one-thumb play.

Controls Overlay: Before drawing katana, show an overlay image describing control scheme (mobile and PC). Example labels in Russian: "Нажмите ✤ для лёгкой атаки, □ для блока". Once dismissed, player gets the katana.

Character Creation Screen: Input name, select family (show family banners with buff icons, e.g. +15% DMG). Show preview of avatar. Simple mobile navigation (arrows or swipe).

Spawn/Revival Screen: Let player set their spawn village (applied each death).

Skill Tree UI: Grid with nodes (Breath styles, Strength, Stamina, special moves). Tapping a node shows name, description, cost in points. Branching tree lines. Accessible via menu.

Breathing Styles Screen: List unlocked styles and locked ones (with "How to unlock" tips).

Quest Log: Scrollable list of active/available quests, with objectives and map markers.

Map: Full-screen regional map with icons (towns, trainers, quest locations, bosses). Zoomable on PC, pinch on mobile.

Inventory: Item slots, currency, equip weapon/amulets. Consumables (potions) quick-access.

Party Panel: Shows party members (health bars, revive option). Button to invite/join party.

Settings: Includes Mobile Control Editor: allow players to reposition on-screen buttons. PC controls listed as reference.
